project.name: llava-for-sensors
project.description: Multimodal fault-prediction model fusing time-series sensor data with vision and language on a frozen Qwen2-VL-2B (LLaVA-for-sensors), trained locally on M2 Max.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the three ablation model variants (SensorsOnly, VisionText, AllThree) that fuse a toy time-series encoder, a frozen Qwen2-VL backbone, and a 4-class classification head for the multimodal fault-prediction experiment.
nodes.languageNotes: Three nn.Module variants share a ClassificationHead and helper functions for Qwen2-VL processor preparation, device routing, and masked-mean pooling of VLM hidden states.

nodes.name: ClassificationHead
nodes.summary: Linear classifier head with LayerNorm over a pooled hidden representation, projecting to n_classes (default 4) for fault classification.

nodes.name: SensorsOnlyModel
nodes.summary: Sensors-only ablation: runs the ToyTSEncoder over the sensor window, mean-pools across patches, and classifies — discarding image and text inputs.

nodes.name: VisionTextModel
nodes.summary: Vision+text ablation: feeds image and prompt text through the frozen Qwen2-VL VLM, masked-mean-pools the hidden states, and classifies — discarding sensor input.

nodes.name: AllThreeModel
nodes.summary: All-three ablation: encodes sensor data via ToyTSEncoder and FusionAdapter into VLM-space tokens, prepends them to the Qwen2-VL input embeddings (extending attention mask and pixel padding accordingly), then masked-mean-pools and classifies.
nodes.languageNotes: Manually splices sensor tokens into the VLM token stream and patches attention_mask, pixel_values, and image_grid_thw to preserve VLM invariants.

nodes.name: _prepare_processor_inputs
nodes.summary: Builds Qwen2-VL processor inputs from an image batch and text prompts, converting tensors to PIL images, applying the chat template, and moving outputs to the target device.

nodes.name: _move_batch_to_device
nodes.summary: Moves a processor-output mapping (dict-like) onto the target device, falling back to per-tensor .to() when no batch-level .to method is available.

nodes.name: _pool_vlm_output
nodes.summary: Pools a Qwen2-VL forward output into a single hidden vector by masked-mean over either last_hidden_state or the final hidden_states tuple entry, raising ValueError when neither is present.

nodes.name: _masked_mean
nodes.summary: Computes the attention-mask-weighted mean of a hidden_state tensor along the sequence dimension, clamping the denominator at 1 to avoid divide-by-zero on empty masks.

nodes.name: encoder.py
nodes.summary: Minimal PatchTST time-series encoder. Patchifies a 2048-sample mono sensor window into 32 non-overlapping 64-sample patches (reshape → nn.Linear(64→512)), adds a learned zero-initialized positional embedding nn.Parameter(1,32,512), and runs 2 nn.TransformerEncoderLayer blocks (8 heads, d_ff=2048, dropout=0.1). Output: (B, 32, 512). Pinned interface contract consumed by FusionAdapter. All trainable. Replaces the Phase 1 toy 1D-CNN; preserves the encoder's input/output shape so models/fusion.py is unchanged.
nodes.languageNotes: Reshape (B, 2048) → (B, 32, 64) using torch view semantics, then nn.Linear(64→512) embeds each non-overlapping 64-sample patch. A learned nn.Parameter(1,32,512) positional embedding is added before two nn.TransformerEncoderLayer blocks (batch_first=True, 8 heads, d_ff=2048, dropout=0.1). The Conv-stride decomposition from Phase 1 is gone — Phase 2 swapped the 1D-CNN backbone for hand-rolled minimal PatchTST while preserving the (B, 32, 512) output contract that FusionAdapter consumes.

nodes.name: ToyTSEncoder
nodes.summary: PatchTST encoder mapping (B, 2048) mono sensor windows to (B, 32, 512) patch embeddings. Class name kept for caller stability across the Phase 1→2 swap; internals are now the hand-rolled minimal PatchTST per .codex-runs/voi-203/spec.md. Forward path: reshape into 32 patches of 64 → patch_embed Linear(64→512) → pos_embed addition → 2-layer TransformerEncoder (8 heads, d_ff=2048, dropout=0.1).

nodes.name: fusion.py
nodes.summary: Cross-attention fusion adapter that maps (B, 32, 512) sensor encoder patches into (B, 16, 1536) fixed sensor tokens at the Qwen2-VL-2B hidden dim, exposing T_SENSOR_TOKENS, D_ENC, and D_VLM constants.
nodes.languageNotes: Learnable query tokens scaled by 0.02 at init; cross-attn key/value come from the linear-projected encoder output with batch_first MHA.

nodes.name: FusionAdapter
nodes.summary: Cross-attention adapter with learnable query tokens that fuses encoder patches into a fixed-length set of VLM sensor tokens, followed by an MLP+LayerNorm refinement.

nodes.name: vlm.py
nodes.summary: Loads Qwen2-VL-2B with all base parameters frozen and PEFT-LoRA adapters attached to q_proj/v_proj for trainable fusion, selecting MPS+fp16 when available and falling back to CPU+fp32 with a warning.
nodes.languageNotes: Re-exports AutoProcessor as VLMProcessor; freezes all parameters before wrapping with LoraConfig(task_type=CAUSAL_LM, target_modules=[q_proj, v_proj]).

nodes.name: load_frozen_vlm_with_lora
nodes.summary: Returns a Qwen2-VL-2B PeftModel with all base params frozen and LoRA adapters (r/alpha/dropout configurable) on q_proj and v_proj, placed on MPS-fp16 if available, otherwise CPU-fp32.

nodes.name: test_encoder.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for ToyTSEncoder (PatchTST after Phase 2). Covers output shape (B,32,512), trainable-parameter budget, NaN/Inf absence on forward, gradient backflow through every named parameter, and the PatchTST-specific invariants: positional-embedding shape (1,32,512), transformer-stack layer count = 2.

nodes.name: test_encoder_backward
nodes.summary: Verifies that every named parameter of ToyTSEncoder receives a non-None gradient after summing the output and backpropagating.

nodes.name: test_fusion.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for FusionAdapter covering output shape (B,16,1536), NaN/Inf absence, backward gradient propagation, and a torch.autograd.gradcheck on a small-double-precision variant.

nodes.name: test_fusion_gradcheck
nodes.summary: Numerical gradient check on a small (d_enc=4, d_vlm=8, t_sensor=2, n_heads=2) double-precision FusionAdapter via torch.autograd.gradcheck.

nodes.name: test_vlm.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for the frozen Qwen2-VL-2B-with-LoRA loader covering load success, base-parameter freezing, LoRA trainability, hidden-size (1536) resolution across PEFT/HF config layouts, and an MPS forward+backward OOM budget check.

nodes.name: _resolve_hidden_size
nodes.summary: Walks a PEFT-wrapped Qwen2-VL model through up to three base_model levels and several config attribute names to extract the underlying hidden_size, accommodating layout drift across transformers/peft versions.

nodes.name: test_vlm_forward_oom_budget
nodes.summary: On MPS-capable boxes, runs a full forward+backward through the frozen Qwen2-VL-2B+LoRA model on a tiny prompt and records pre/post driver-allocated memory to enforce the M2-Max OOM budget.

nodes.name: dataset.py
nodes.summary: Torch Dataset wrapper around the synthetic generator that yields sensor/image/text/label tuples for training and evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic Dataset[tuple[...]] typing carries the four-modality tuple shape through PyTorch's DataLoader.

nodes.name: ToyDataset
nodes.summary: Map-style PyTorch Dataset that wraps a list of SyntheticSample dicts (or generates them from a seed) and returns (sensor_tensor, image_tensor, text, label) tuples on indexing.

nodes.name: synthetic.py
nodes.summary: Synthetic cross-modal toy data generator producing sensor waveforms, RGB images, and text descriptions across four classes with deliberate cross-modal ambiguity for fusion experiments.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses np.random.default_rng for seed-deterministic generation; TypedDict declares the multimodal sample shape.

nodes.name: SyntheticSample
nodes.summary: TypedDict declaring the shape of one synthetic toy sample: sensor ndarray, image ndarray, text string, and integer label.

nodes.name: _sample_sensor
nodes.summary: Generates a 2048-sample sinusoidal sensor trace whose frequency band depends on the class id, with additive Gaussian noise to make the modality non-trivial.

nodes.name: _sample_image
nodes.summary: Generates a 224x224x3 RGB image whose color signature encodes the class id, deliberately overlapping pairs of classes so vision alone is ambiguous.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that produces a balanced, shuffled list of SyntheticSample dicts for the requested sample count and seed, calling the per-modality samplers.

nodes.name: _balanced_labels
nodes.summary: Produces an evenly distributed list of class labels across N_CLASSES for a requested sample count; raises if n is not a multiple of the class count.

nodes.name: test_synthetic.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive pytest suite for the synthetic generator and ToyDataset, including determinism, class balance, modality-ambiguity probes, and a stratified-split + manual TF-IDF logistic-regression baseline that proves cross-modal fusion is required.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a from-scratch logistic-regression and macro-F1 implementation as a deterministic fallback when sklearn output drifts.

nodes.name: test_generate_default_shapes_and_types
nodes.summary: Verifies generate() returns the expected per-sample shapes/dtypes across the four modalities and that invalid sample counts raise.

nodes.name: test_generate_is_deterministic_for_seed
nodes.summary: Confirms generate() with the same seed produces identical outputs and that a different seed actually diverges, guarding the determinism contract.

nodes.name: test_toy_dataset_wraps_samples
nodes.summary: Tests ToyDataset wraps a pre-generated sample list, returns tensors of the right dtype, and preserves the underlying data values.

nodes.name: test_toy_dataset_can_generate_from_seed
nodes.summary: Tests ToyDataset's seed-based constructor path produces identical contents to a manually generated sample list at the same seed.

nodes.name: test_cross_modal_required_property
nodes.summary: Quantitative baseline test asserting that no single modality (sensor/image/text) alone reaches the macro-F1 ceiling, motivating the cross-modal fusion architecture.

nodes.name: test_vision_text_pair_remains_ambiguous
nodes.summary: Verifies the deliberate ambiguity property: vision+text together still cannot perfectly separate the four classes, so the sensor modality is genuinely informative.

nodes.name: _stratified_split
nodes.summary: Stratified train/test index split helper using sklearn when available and falling back to a hand-rolled per-class shuffle for determinism.

nodes.name: _text_features
nodes.summary: Builds TF-IDF features for the text modality using sklearn when available, otherwise falls back to a manual bag-of-words/IDF approximation.

nodes.name: _manual_text_features
nodes.summary: Pure-numpy bag-of-words text featurizer used as a sklearn-free fallback to keep the cross-modal baseline test deterministic.

nodes.name: _fit_score
nodes.summary: Standardizes features and fits a logistic-regression classifier (sklearn LogisticRegression or manual fallback), returning macro-F1 on the held-out split.

nodes.name: _fit_lr
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled multinomial logistic-regression trainer using batch gradient descent, used when sklearn is unavailable for reproducible test scoring.

nodes.name: _macro_f1
nodes.summary: Computes macro-averaged F1 over n_classes from one-vs-rest precision/recall, used by the cross-modal baseline tests.

nodes.name: ablation.py
nodes.summary: Driver script for the three-condition (sensors-only, vision+text, all-three) ablation experiment: generates data, trains each condition across seeds, and writes a results CSV.

nodes.name: run_ablation
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full ablation: generates balanced data, stratified-splits train/val, iterates conditions and seeds, calls train_one_run, and writes the results CSV.

nodes.name: _build_model
nodes.summary: Factory dispatching the three ablation conditions to SensorsOnlyModel, VisionTextModel, or AllThreeModel.

nodes.name: _stratified_split
nodes.summary: Stratified 80/20 train/val split that groups samples by class and interleaves them to preserve order-independent class balance.

nodes.name: _main
nodes.summary: CLI argument parser entry point that exposes n-seeds, n-epochs, output path, samples-per-class, and device flags for run_ablation.

nodes.name: headline.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point and CSV-to-headline driver that reads the ablation results CSV, validates the 3-conditions x 5-seeds shape, invokes the bootstrap headline computation, renders the SVG, and raises PhaseAcceptanceError when the gate criteria fail.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses argparse for CLI plumbing; collects failure reasons into a list before raising a single composite PhaseAcceptanceError so all gate violations surface in one error message.

nodes.name: headline_figure.py
nodes.summary: Statistical core for the phase headline: computes per-condition means, bootstrap confidence intervals, paired-bootstrap p-values, and renders a deterministic matplotlib SVG bar chart with explicit rect markers for downstream validation.
nodes.languageNotes: All RNG flows through numpy.random.default_rng for determinism; SVG is post-processed via xml.etree.ElementTree to guarantee a stable number of <rect> markers regardless of matplotlib version drift.

nodes.name: test_ablation.py
nodes.summary: Integration tests for the ablation pipeline and headline acceptance gate: stubs Qwen-VL submodules to verify 4-class logit shape and pixel-value forwarding, exercises run_ablation end-to-end with a tmp CSV, and asserts the gate rejects malformed or non-significant result CSVs.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of stub torch.nn.Module subclasses (_StubVLM, _StubEmbedding) to avoid loading the real Qwen2-VL weights; pytest tmp_path fixtures isolate CSV side-effects per test.

nodes.name: test_headline.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the headline statistics: validates fusion-wins detection, flat (no-difference) negative-result protocol, strict 3x5 shape enforcement, bootstrap CI numerical bounds, SVG output structure, non-finite input rejection, and rendering determinism.

nodes.name: PhaseAcceptanceError
nodes.summary: Domain-specific exception raised when the phase headline acceptance gate fails - used by the CLI driver to surface composite gate-violation messages.

nodes.name: run_headline_from_csv
nodes.summary: Top-level orchestrator that reads results CSV, computes headline statistics, renders the SVG, and aggregates all gate failures (NaN per-condition CIs, missing significance, p-value too high) into a single PhaseAcceptanceError.

nodes.name: _read_results_csv
nodes.summary: Parses the ablation results CSV, validates per-condition seed-uniqueness and the strict 3-conditions x 5-seeds shape, and returns a stacked numpy array indexed by condition.

nodes.name: compute_headline
nodes.summary: Core headline computation: validates the 3x5 results array (strict mode), computes per-condition means and bootstrap 95% CIs, runs a paired bootstrap on vision-vs-fusion to get a p-value, and returns the structured headline dict consumed by render_svg and the gate.

nodes.name: render_svg
nodes.summary: Renders the deterministic headline SVG bar chart with error bars and a fusion p-value annotation, then post-processes the output to guarantee a stable count of <rect> markers for downstream visual-validation checks.

nodes.name: _bootstrap_ci
nodes.summary: Computes a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for a sample by resampling with replacement n_resamples times and taking the 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the resampled means.

nodes.name: _paired_bootstrap_p
nodes.summary: Two-sided paired bootstrap p-value: resamples the per-seed differences between two conditions and returns the fraction of resampled means whose absolute value exceeds the observed absolute mean difference.

nodes.name: _validate_results
nodes.summary: Validates that the input results are a non-empty 2-D numpy array containing only finite values, raising ValueError on any violation.

nodes.name: _ensure_svg_rect_markers
nodes.summary: Post-processes the saved SVG to guarantee at least expected_count <rect> elements exist, appending invisible padding rects when matplotlib's output undercounts - stabilises the SVG schema for downstream snapshot tests.

nodes.name: _cis_dont_fully_overlap
nodes.summary: Pure helper checking whether two confidence intervals are disjoint enough for the headline to claim a difference (returns True when the CIs do not strictly overlap).

nodes.name: _StubVLM
nodes.summary: Lightweight torch.nn.Module stub mimicking the Qwen2-VL backbone surface used by VisionTextModel / AllThreeModel - provides a deterministic embedding table and a forward returning the namespace shape models.py expects.

nodes.name: _StubProcessor
nodes.summary: Test double for the Qwen2-VL processor returning minimal input_ids/attention_mask tensors - lets vision/text model paths execute without loading the real tokenizer.

nodes.name: _StubProcessorWithPixelValues
nodes.summary: Extended stub processor that also emits pixel_values derived from the input sensor tensor, used to verify AllThreeModel forwards both image and sensor channels through the VLM.

nodes.name: _StubVLMWithPixelValues
nodes.summary: Stub VLM whose forward incorporates pixel_values into the hidden state, allowing the test suite to assert that AllThreeModel actually pipes the image branch through.

nodes.name: test_models_have_4class_logits
nodes.summary: Asserts that SensorsOnlyModel, VisionTextModel, and AllThreeModel all produce (batch, 4) logits - locking the fault-classification head shape across the three ablation variants.

nodes.name: test_all_three_pixel_values_forwarded
nodes.summary: Spies on the stub VLM's forward to confirm AllThreeModel passes non-None, non-zero pixel_values through, preventing a silent regression where the image branch is dropped.

nodes.name: test_run_ablation_writes_csv
nodes.summary: End-to-end smoke test: runs run_ablation on tiny tensors and asserts the resulting CSV exists with the expected row count and finite metric values.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_rejects_failing_results
nodes.summary: Negative-path test: fabricates a CSV where vision and fusion are identical and asserts run_headline_from_csv raises PhaseAcceptanceError.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_rejects_no_significance
nodes.summary: Patches compute_headline to force a non-significant p-value (>0.05) and confirms the CLI driver raises PhaseAcceptanceError citing the significance failure.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_rejects_wrong_seed_count
nodes.summary: Confirms the CSV reader rejects a 3x4 result matrix - the gate must enforce exactly 5 seeds per condition.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_rejects_duplicate_seeds
nodes.summary: Writes a CSV with duplicate seed IDs across conditions and verifies the reader rejects it - guarding against accidental seed reuse that would invalidate the paired-bootstrap assumption.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_rejects_duplicate_seed_ids_per_condition
nodes.summary: Asserts the CSV reader rejects a result file containing duplicate seed IDs within a single condition.

nodes.name: test_headline_gate_accepts_passing_results
nodes.summary: Positive-path test using a hand-tuned CSV where fusion clearly beats vision; asserts the gate accepts the input and produces an SVG with bootstrap CIs and p-value < 0.05.

nodes.name: _write_fake_csv
nodes.summary: Test helper that materializes a synthetic results CSV (condition, seed_idx, metric) on disk for the gate-rejection tests.

nodes.name: test_known_good_fusion_wins
nodes.summary: Asserts compute_headline detects a real fusion-vs-vision advantage with a small synthetic 3x5 matrix where fusion means are visibly higher than vision means.

nodes.name: test_known_flat_no_difference
nodes.summary: Negative-result protocol: when vision and fusion are statistically identical, compute_headline must report no significant difference rather than fabricating an effect.

nodes.name: test_strict_mode_rejects_non_3x5
nodes.summary: Confirms strict=True raises on shapes other than (3,5) while strict=False allows it - locking the phase contract for the gate path.

nodes.name: test_negative_result_protocol
nodes.summary: Verifies the headline doesn't claim significance when the per-seed differences average to zero, even if the means look mildly different - guarding against false positives.

nodes.name: test_bootstrap_ci_numerical_correctness
nodes.summary: Numerical sanity check: confirms each condition's 95% bootstrap CI lies inside the [min, max] envelope of its inputs - catches a class of off-by-one or percentile mis-indexing bugs.

nodes.name: test_svg_output
nodes.summary: End-to-end SVG check: renders the headline figure, parses it with ElementTree, and asserts root tag, presence of bars (>=3 rects), and the p-value annotation text.

nodes.name: test_non_finite_input_rejected
nodes.summary: Asserts compute_headline raises on inputs containing NaN or +/- infinity, preventing silent propagation of bad values into the bootstrap.

nodes.name: test_svg_render_is_deterministic
nodes.summary: Renders the same headline twice and asserts byte-for-byte identical SVG output - encodes the determinism contract from the phase spec.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Train package barrel that re-exports the public training entry points (TrainResult, train_one_run) from loop.py for ergonomic imports.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__.py acting as a re-export surface.

nodes.name: loop.py
nodes.summary: Minimal end-to-end training loop for llava-for-sensors: orchestrates AdamW + cosine LR scheduling, gradient accumulation, macro-F1 validation, JSONL step/epoch logging, peak-memory tracking, and best-checkpoint persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch nn.Module-agnostic loop using DataLoader + AdamW + CosineAnnealingLR; MPS-aware device resolution and memory accounting; private helpers prefixed with underscore.

nodes.name: test_loop.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite exercising train_one_run across dataclass shape, smoke convergence, checkpointing, JSONL logging schema, seed determinism, gradient accumulation cadence, macro-F1 averaging, and ceil-not-floor scheduler T_max behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tiny in-memory _TinyLinearModel + _TinyDataset fixtures; gates expensive smoke tests behind LLAVA_FOR_SENSORS_RUN_SMOKE env var.

nodes.name: TrainResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing the full result of a training run: final and best macro-F1, best epoch, per-step loss trace, per-epoch val F1, peak device memory, and checkpoint path.

nodes.name: train_one_run
nodes.summary: Drives a complete training run: seeds RNGs, builds DataLoaders, sets up AdamW + cosine scheduler, executes the gradient-accumulated train/eval epochs, writes JSONL logs, persists best checkpoint, and returns a TrainResult.

nodes.name: _collate_batch
nodes.summary: Custom DataLoader collate_fn that stacks sensor tensors, image tensors, and label tensors while preserving raw text prompts as a list.

nodes.name: _evaluate_macro_f1
nodes.summary: Runs the model in eval mode over a validation DataLoader under torch.no_grad and returns the macro-F1 across all classes.

nodes.name: _macro_f1
nodes.summary: Computes unweighted macro-F1 over all N_CLASSES classes from predicted and target label arrays, handling absent classes via a zero-score fallback.

nodes.name: _save_best_checkpoint
nodes.summary: Persists the current best model: prefers HuggingFace save_pretrained when available, otherwise falls back to torch.save of state_dict.

nodes.name: _TinyLinearModel
nodes.summary: Minimal nn.Module test fixture: single Linear head over flattened sensor input, used to drive train_one_run cheaply without the full multimodal stack.

nodes.name: _TinyDataset
nodes.summary: In-memory torch Dataset fixture yielding deterministic (sensor, image, text, label) tuples for unit-testing train_one_run.

nodes.name: test_train_one_run_returns_result
nodes.summary: Verifies train_one_run returns a properly populated TrainResult with non-empty loss/val traces on a trivial dataset.

nodes.name: test_loss_decreases_on_toy_smoke
nodes.summary: Smoke test gated by LLAVA_FOR_SENSORS_RUN_SMOKE: confirms training reduces mean loss across epochs on the toy dataset.

nodes.name: test_checkpoint_saved_on_improvement
nodes.summary: Verifies that a checkpoint file is written to disk when validation F1 improves during training (gated smoke).

nodes.name: test_jsonl_logging_emits_step_and_epoch_events
nodes.summary: Asserts the JSONL log contains both step-level and epoch-level events with the expected schema keys.

nodes.name: test_determinism_same_seed
nodes.summary: Runs train_one_run twice with the same seed and confirms per-step loss traces match within a small tolerance, gating reproducibility.

nodes.name: test_grad_accum_steps_optimizer_every_n_batches
nodes.summary: Verifies gradient accumulation cadence: optimizer.step() fires every grad_accum batches, asserted via JSONL log inspection.

nodes.name: test_scheduler_t_max_is_ceil_not_floor
nodes.summary: Guards a known-arithmetic correctness invariant: CosineAnnealingLR T_max uses math.ceil over partial accumulation windows so the schedule does not under-count optimizer steps.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Bounded-worker operating contract for Codex exec workers — hard rules on scope, no-network, no-git, faithful transcription of Claude-authored content, plus UI/styling and test-value contracts earned from past fan-in misses.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Claude's operating contract as director/spec-author/scope-gate/final-integrator — spec authoring discipline, autonomy boundary, per-packet build loop, runtime-verification doctrine, internal review loop, file-scope contract, and recurring failure classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Long-form load-bearing doctrine; every section corresponds to an automated gate or a real past failure mode.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative project plan: pre-registered headline-figure contract (3 modality conditions × 5 seeds, macro-F1 with bootstrap CIs), doctrine and cadence, framework/stack decisions, and Phase 0–7 plan with per-phase acceptance gates.
nodes.languageNotes: Source-of-truth document — packet specs must pull-quote from this per the CLAUDE.md spec-authoring discipline.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview README — thesis (sensors+vision+text beats vision+text on CWRU fault prediction), reviewer entry points table, headline-figure and demo placeholders, doctrine one-liner, and local-only repro instructions.

nodes.name: RUNNING_NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Append-only lab journal: per-phase decisions, dead ends, memory/timing measurements, blockers. Phase 0 done (10 packets + 2 META PRs). Phase 1 done — the headline ablation gate passed: sensors-only 0.436 / vision+text 0.416 / all-three 0.867 (paired-bootstrap p=0.0002, gap=45.1pp, above the >15pp PLAN.md §1(e) threshold). Captures the r17 false-positive revert (codex bot flagged an XOR error in input_ids+inputs_embeds that doesn't fire — manual-scatter fix broke the working path), the seed-4 dead-init outlier, the toy dataset's deliberately-redundant vision-text axes, and the GH-private-repo flip. Memory/timing instrumentation gap (peak RAM, time-per-epoch) carried to Phase 2. Phase 2 packets (PatchTST encoder swap + architecture/component.c4 update) staged for dispatch.

nodes.name: TECH_REPORT.md
nodes.summary: Phase 6 mini-arXiv tech report skeleton — abstract, method (frozen Qwen2-VL-2B + LoRA + time-series encoder + fusion adapter), CWRU data, ablations including the pre-registered headline figure, and reproducibility section.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Minimal private npm package manifest declaring likec4 as the sole runtime dependency and exposing the `build:c4` script that compiles LikeC4 architecture sources into SVGs under docs/architecture.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project manifest for llava-for-sensors — requires Python ≥3.11, declares the ML stack (torch ≥2.4, transformers, peft, accelerate, gradio) plus the pytest+ruff dev group, with uv as the managed toolchain.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses uv's managed python-preference and PEP 735 dependency-groups (dev group) — no setup.py/requirements.txt.

nodes.name: compaction-sidecar.sh
nodes.summary: PreCompact/PostCompact Claude Code hook that writes durable JSON breadcrumbs (resume-pointer.json, last-compaction.json) capturing git state and Linear project pointers so a post-compaction SessionStart reflex can reorient.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash wrapper around an inline python3 heredoc; payload passed via env (HOOK_IN) to avoid stdin collision with the heredoc, and JSON built with json.dump to escape arbitrary git output safely.

nodes.name: delegation-sidecar.sh
nodes.summary: PostToolUse hook that emits a throttled (5-minute) soft-compass reminder of standing delegation/orchestration principles whenever Claude edits a file, with a gentle aside when the edit touches implementation code paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Fail-open shell hook with jq-then-python3 fallback for both payload parsing and JSON output, plus recursion guards (skips hooks/.claude/hooks edits) and a stamp-file throttle.

nodes.name: session-recovery.sh
nodes.summary: SessionStart hook wrapper that delegates to session-recovery.py for context-recovery JSON, but guarantees a loud hardcoded fallback payload (with project Linear pointers and RESUME-ACK contract) so the reflex can never silently vanish.
nodes.languageNotes: Honors a deliberate /clear source by exiting empty; otherwise either the python helper output or the hardcoded fallback is always emitted.

nodes.name: check-prereqs.sh
nodes.summary: Prerequisite verifier for the dev/build/test loop; prints one ✓/✗ line per check and exits non-zero if any required tool is missing or below the required version. Also enforces a regression check that no runtime script reads from the stale .template.answers file (VOI-189).

nodes.name: version_ge
nodes.summary: Semantic version comparison helper that returns success when the first argument is greater-than-or-equal to the required version, used by every tool-version assertion in the verifier.

nodes.name: check-shell-syntax.sh
nodes.summary: Runs bash -n syntax-check over staged shell-script blobs (via git show :FILE) so the pre-commit gate sees exactly what would be committed rather than the working-tree content. Also flags a common Python-in-single-quoted-shell apostrophe pitfall.

nodes.name: codex-review.sh
nodes.summary: Internal stateless adversarial reviewer that runs a stronger Codex model at xhigh reasoning against `git diff base...HEAD` and writes the verdict to .codex-runs/<run-id>/review.md. Acts as the pre-PR backstop so the GitHub @codex bot becomes a true backstop rather than the primary net.

nodes.name: codex-run.sh
nodes.summary: Canonical codex-exec dispatch helper that builds .codex-runs/<run-id>/ artifacts, invokes codex exec for either an explorer or worker role with locked-down flags, and captures the transcript plus git diff so Claude can audit the worker's output. Production code only enters the repo through this script.

nodes.name: codex-runs-gc.sh
nodes.summary: Garbage-collects the gitignored .codex-runs/ directory using a merged-or-gone protocol: only removes a family when its loop-status is terminal and no live branch/worktree still references it. Supports --self-test (hermetic), --dry-run, and --aggressive modes.

nodes.name: slug_protected
nodes.summary: Decides whether a run-family slug is still protected by a live, non-merged local or remote branch — the safety check that prevents the GC from collecting in-flight work even in --aggressive mode.

nodes.name: impl-precommit-scope.sh
nodes.summary: Validates that staged or committed diff paths stay inside the implementer's allowed write scope. Operates in --cached pre-commit mode (role allowlist only) or in --base/--worktree/--scope-file mode for Claude's authoritative pre-PR and final-head re-gate enforcing both the per-packet allowlist and the role allowlist.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements anchored prefix matching (rel === p or rel.startsWith(p + '/')) per the CLAUDE.md rule against substring-anywhere scope matchers.

nodes.name: in_packet_scope
nodes.summary: Tests whether a given relative path falls inside the per-packet allowlist using anchored prefix and exact-file matching — the load-bearing predicate behind the scope gate.

nodes.name: queue-scan.sh
nodes.summary: Parallelization-gate queue scanner (VOI-229) that lists Phase-0 packets dispatchable right now — not merged, no existing branch, and all declared dependencies content-available (merged or stacked). Companion to hooks/schedule-wakeup-guard.mjs, which uses its exit code to deny ScheduleWakeup when there is work to dispatch.

nodes.name: review-gate.sh
nodes.summary: Codex review-gate helper for the GitHub delivery flow with status/threads/reply/resolve/wait subcommands. `wait` runs the two-phase eye-emoji loop — post @codex review, wait for 👀 ack, then poll until a verdict comment or thread lands — so callers don't own retry discipline.
nodes.languageNotes: Matches both REST author login `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and GraphQL author login `chatgpt-codex-connector` to avoid the silent-no-match failure noted in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.name: worktree-new.sh
nodes.summary: Creates a per-packet implementer git worktree with a real APFS-cloned node_modules so the worktree is immediately bootable inside Codex's workspace-write sandbox. Bare-NAME arg 2 collects worktrees under <parent>/.llava-for-sensors-worktrees/<name>.

nodes.name: implementer.md
nodes.summary: Implementer subagent operating contract specifying the strict no-direct-code rule, codex-exec dispatch protocol, /codex:review loop, commit/push/PR gating, and eye-emoji review iteration cycle the impl must follow per packet.
nodes.languageNotes: 17 sections; load-bearing operating contract referenced by CLAUDE.md.

tour.title: Project Pitch & Reviewer Entry
tour.description: Start with the README. It states the core thesis — that bolting a small trainable fusion adapter onto a frozen Qwen2-VL-2B lets time-series sensor data flow into the VLM's token space alongside vision and text — and points at the reviewer entry points (headline figure, PLAN.md, RUNNING_NOTES.md, TECH_REPORT.md, component.c4). Treat it as the project's table of contents: every later step in this tour expands one of the cells the README sketches.

tour.title: Delivery Contract & Phase Plan
tour.description: PLAN.md is the authoritative project plan: it pre-registers the headline figure (3 modality conditions × 5 seeds, macro-F1 with bootstrap CIs), declares the doctrine and cadence, and lays out Phases 0–7 with per-phase acceptance gates. The lab journal in RUNNING_NOTES.md captures what actually happened phase-by-phase, including dead ends and timing measurements — together they make the project's progress legible without reading any source.

tour.title: Model-Internals Architecture
tour.description: Before diving into code, view the LikeC4 component diagram. It decomposes the system into trainable vs frozen subcomponents (ToyTSEncoder, FusionAdapter, frozen Qwen2-VL-2B + LoRA) with the exact tensor shapes flowing between them — this is the picture the next several steps fill in file by file. Reading this first means you'll recognize each shape (B,32,512), (B,16,1536), (B,4) as it appears in the modules.
tour.languageLesson: LikeC4 is architecture-as-code: .c4 sources declare model elements (containers, components, relations) and a TypeScript-based DSL renders them to SVG. The committed source diffs cleanly in PRs, unlike opaque binary diagrams.

tour.title: Synthetic Data Generator
tour.description: The data layer is the experiment's foundation: data/synthetic.py emits sensor waveforms, RGB images, and text descriptions across four classes with deliberate cross-modal ambiguity (no single modality is enough to classify), and data/dataset.py wraps it in a PyTorch Dataset that yields (sensor, image, text, label) tuples for training and evaluation. The 'cross-modal ambiguity' design is what makes the ablation in Step 10 meaningful — if any one modality solved the task alone, fusion would prove nothing.

tour.title: Evidence Gate on Data
tour.description: Per CLAUDE.md's 'evidence — really produced by real logic' doctrine, every claim the data layer makes needs a test that proves it. data/test_synthetic.py covers determinism, class balance, and modality-ambiguity probes, and crucially trains a stratified-split TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline that demonstrates no single modality solves the task — the empirical anchor for why fusion matters.
tour.languageLesson: Pytest determinism tests typically (1) seed all RNGs (numpy, torch, random), (2) run the generator twice, and (3) assert tensor equality. Without this, downstream training noise is indistinguishable from upstream sampling noise.

tour.title: Time-Series Encoder & Fusion Adapter
tour.description: These are the two trainable modules on top of the frozen VLM. models/encoder.py is the minimal PatchTST encoder (Phase 2 swap from the original toy 1D-CNN): reshape 2048 samples into 32 patches of 64, nn.Linear(64→512) per-patch, learned positional embedding, two nn.TransformerEncoderLayer blocks. Output shape (B, 32, 512). models/fusion.py is the cross-attention fusion adapter that compresses those 32 sensor patches into 16 query tokens at the VLM hidden dim. Both are trainable.
tour.languageLesson: Cross-attention adapters are the standard trick for stitching a new modality onto a frozen LLM: a small trainable Q/K/V projection conditions the new modality's tokens on the LLM's hidden dim, so the rest of the model can attend to them as if they were native.

tour.title: Frozen Qwen2-VL-2B + LoRA
tour.description: models/vlm.py is the third pillar of the architecture: it loads Qwen2-VL-2B with all base parameters frozen and PEFT-LoRA adapters attached to q_proj/v_proj. The freezing is what makes the project feasible on an M2 Max — only the LoRA adapters, the encoder, and the fusion module actually receive gradients. The loader also handles device-and-dtype selection (MPS+fp16 when available, CPU+fp32 with a warning) so the same code runs on the dev laptop and any CI fallback.
tour.languageLesson: PEFT-LoRA adds low-rank ΔW = BA matrices to selected projection layers. Only B and A train (typically <1% of base params), while the original W stays frozen — drastically reducing memory and making large pretrained backbones trainable on consumer hardware.

tour.title: Model Tests — Shapes, Freezing, Memory Budget
tour.description: The three model test files enforce the architectural contracts the diagram in Step 3 promised. test_encoder.py asserts output shape (B,32,512), parameter budget, and gradient flow. test_fusion.py adds a torch.autograd.gradcheck on a small double-precision variant — a strong correctness signal for a custom attention path. test_vlm.py covers load success, base-parameter freezing (LoRA-only trainability), hidden-size 1536 resolution across PEFT/HF config layouts, and an MPS forward+backward OOM budget check that catches regressions in memory footprint.

tour.title: The Training Loop
tour.description: train/loop.py is the minimal end-to-end orchestrator: AdamW + cosine LR scheduling, gradient accumulation, macro-F1 validation, JSONL step/epoch logging, peak-memory tracking, and best-checkpoint persistence. Its companion test_loop.py exercises smoke convergence, checkpointing, the JSONL log schema, seed determinism, gradient-accumulation cadence, and a ceil-not-floor scheduler T_max edge case — every claim the loop makes is independently verified.
tour.languageLesson: Gradient accumulation simulates a larger batch by summing gradients across N micro-batches before calling optimizer.step(). T_max for a cosine schedule must be the count of optimizer steps (post-accumulation), not the count of forward passes — a common off-by-N bug the test_loop ceil-not-floor case catches.

tour.title: Three-Condition Ablation
tour.description: This is the heart of the experiment. eval/models.py defines the three ablation model variants — SensorsOnly, VisionText, AllThree — that share the PatchTST encoder (still imported as ToyTSEncoder by class name) and a 4-class classification head over the frozen Qwen2-VL backbone. eval/ablation.py is the driver that generates data, trains each condition across 5 seeds, and writes a results CSV. eval/test_ablation.py stubs the Qwen-VL submodules so the integration test runs offline and asserts both 4-class logit shape and end-to-end CSV output — the path from 'model variants exist' to 'we have empirical numbers to act on'.

tour.title: Headline Statistics & Acceptance Gate
tour.description: eval/headline_figure.py is the statistical core: per-condition means, bootstrap confidence intervals, paired-bootstrap p-values, and a deterministic matplotlib SVG bar chart with explicit rect markers. eval/headline.py is the CLI driver that reads the ablation CSV, validates the pre-registered 3×5 shape, invokes the bootstrap, renders the SVG, and raises PhaseAcceptanceError if the all-three vs vision+text gap fails the acceptance gate. test_headline.py covers fusion-wins detection, the flat-negative-result protocol, CI numerical bounds, and SVG output structure. Phase 1's reported macro-F1 = 0.867 vs 0.416 (p = 0.0002) is what this pipeline produced — and refused to fake.
tour.languageLesson: A paired bootstrap p-value resamples with the same indices across both conditions, so it tests whether the gap exceeds within-seed variance — much stronger than two independent bootstraps because it controls for seed-to-seed difficulty drift.

tour.title: Agent Operating Doctrine
tour.description: Finally, the workflow doctrine that produced every commit in this repo. CLAUDE.md is the director contract — spec authoring, file-scope contract, autonomy boundary, runtime-verification gate. AGENTS.md is the Codex worker contract — bounded transcription, no-network, no-git. implementer.md is the impl subagent's protocol — codex-exec dispatch, /codex:review loop, eye-emoji review iteration. write-scope-guard.mjs is the wall behind those rules: a PreToolUse hook that denies Edit/Write/MultiEdit on production code so Claude can never bypass the dispatch-to-codex invariant by accident. Understanding these explains why every PR in this repo looks structurally the same.
